Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 22-Dec-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  DIGITAL SYSTEM DESIGN [CSE_2123]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                         Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Design a sequential circuit with two JK flip-flops A and B and two inputs E and F. If E = 0, the circuit (5)  
  remains in the same state regardless of the value of F . When E = 1 and F = 1, the circuit goes  
  A)           through the state transitions from 00 to 01, to 10, to 11, back to 00, and repeats. When E = 1 and F  
  = 0, the circuit goes through the state transitions from 00 to 11, to 10, to 01, back to 00, and  
  repeats.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Show the transistor-level diagram for a two-input CMOS NAND gate. Determine why the NMOS                  (3)  
  transistors are placed in series in the pull-down network, while the PMOS transistors are placed in  
  parallel in the pull-up network to achieve the NAND logic function.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  $$C)           Simplify the function F(a,b,c,d) = IIM(1,3,5,8,9,11,15) + D(2,13) using K-map to obtain the minimum (2)$$  
  cost SOP expression and draw the circuit.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                Apply the concept of the Carry-Lookahead Adder (CLA) by deriving the general expressions for the (5)  
  Carry Generate (G_i), Carry Propagate (P_i), and the output carry (C i+1) for a single stage. Apply  
  A)           these concepts to write the specific logical expressions for the output carries C_1 and C_2 in terms  
  of the initial carry C_0 and the corresponding G and P terms. Explain why the CLA is faster than a  
  Ripple Carry Adder.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Design a 4-to-1 multiplexer using only 2-to-1 multiplexers. Implement this design in Verilog HDL          (3)  
  and simulate the circuit.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Illustrate a circuit using full adders to find the no. of 1's in a three-bit unsigned number.             (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                Illustrate the synchronous counter with the following repeated binary sequence: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.      (5)  
  Use JK flip-flops. Check if it is self-correcting or not.  
  A)  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Apply the necessary external logic connections to a JK Flip-Flop to convert it into an equivalent T    (3)  
  Flip-Flop. Explain the simple modification required on the J and K inputs to achieve the toggle  
  function when needed.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Apply the understanding of sequential circuits to design a basic RS latch using NOR gates.             (2)  
  Demonstrate its working with a detailed circuit diagram and truth table.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)              Construct an ASM chart for the pseudo code of a bit counter and explain it.                            (5)  
  
  
  A)                                                      Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         Determine the operation of a Serial-In, Parallel-Out (SIPO) Shift Register. Explain the specific steps (3)  
  (in terms of clock cycles) required to load an 8-bit data word into the register and how the data is  
  then accessed at the output terminals.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Apply the design principles of an Asynchronous (Ripple) Counter and the operational constraints of (2)  
  a Positive Edge-Triggered T Flip-Flop to implement a 4-bit UP counter in Verilog.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)              Draw the standard symbol and the truth table for a Tri-state Driver. Apply the Tri-state Driver to (5)  
  explain how the outputs of two registers R1 and R2 are safely connected to a common bus line with  
  A)         the help of a diagram.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)         Design a three-bit counter that counts in the sequence 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 0.                            (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)         Show the relationship between the number of states N generated by a simple ring counter and the        (2)  
  number of flip-flops k used.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  
  -----End-----
